headline: DSWD Disaster Assistance Surpasses ₱1.09 Billion for Monsoon- and Cyclone-Affected Communities
seoTitle: DSWD Disaster Aid Tops ₱1.09 Billion | FMB News
seoDescription: DSWD says assistance for communities affected by the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones has surpassed ₱1.09 billion as relief operations continue.
deck: The social welfare department says cumulative assistance has crossed ₱1.09 billion as food, non-food and financial support continues for communities affected by the monsoon and recent cyclones.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Social Welfare and Development says the value of assistance provided to communities affected by the enhanced southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones has surpassed ₱1.09 billion.

A DSWD Disaster Response Operations Management, Information and Communication report cited in current reporting says the agency had distributed 1.66 million family food packs, 13,864 non-food items, 22,993 ready-to-eat food items and ₱2.76 million in financial assistance as of 6:00 AM Saturday.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The relief operation covers communities affected by the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng. DSWD also reported maintaining nationwide standby stocks, including 3.79 million family food packs, to support continuing operations.

The approved newsroom brief contained different sub-breakdowns for food packs and direct cash assistance. FMB News therefore uses the independently reproduced DROMIC figures for those components while retaining the verified overall assistance milestone.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Large disaster-response totals are useful only when the underlying supplies reach affected households. Food-pack availability, logistics capacity and replenishment levels determine how quickly the government can respond if another weather system renews flooding.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch DSWD's succeeding DROMIC reports for updated assistance totals, remaining displaced families, warehouse inventories and any new pre-positioning ahead of additional monsoon rainfall.
